source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Q4 CY2024 earnings commentary: 'Exports account for only 10% of the business mix' and 'exports grew 23%' YoY; AR narrative frames this as 'local for local' manufacturing with world-class labor-arbitrage advantages, not an explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification thesis. Revenue growth attributed mainly to domestic data center orders and EPC customers, with some 'growth in export markets within the Distribution Solutions division.'

United Spirits (Diageo India) is overwhelmingly domestic-focused; search summaries reference only limited 'exports of certain brands and participation in global travel retail' with no percentage disclosed and no diversification/China+1 framing found.

crude_exposure.evidence: FY25 gross margin of 42.1% was down ~322bps YoY on 'commodity inflation impacting Glass & ENA'; separately, packaging cost commentary noted glass bottles up 11-17%, paper cartons ~100%, and petrochemical-derived PET resin/caps up 30-50% and 15-20% respectively, with CFO citing a 1.25-1.5pp gross-margin hit (~₹40 crore) per quarter from packaging inflation.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company markets its CDMO arm as 'Navin Molecular,' positioned to let customers 'build a geographically diverse supply chain that operates to internationally recognized standards for quality, safety and the environment' — export-momentum/diversification framing, though not an explicit 'China+1' label. Company exports contracted molecules to Bayer CropScience (~INR 1,600mn in FY24/FY25) and holds ~22% share of India's fluorochemicals market. Note: fluorspar, its key feedstock, is itself sourced globally with China as the dominant producer — an import-dependency risk in the opposite direction.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution reported at 77% of revenue in Q4 FY25 (vs. ~40% cited for Q3 FY25, indicating quarterly variability); no explicit USD-denominated revenue % or hedging policy disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is a domestic diagnostics services provider (~280 labs, ~5,700 collection centers across India); no export business or China+1/supply-chain narrative found.

rural.evidence: 'Tier-III and beyond' cities/towns contribute approximately 3% of Dr Lal PathLabs' revenues as of FY25, but are growing faster (17% 4-year revenue CAGR) than the company's overall revenue CAGR (14%) over the same period; FY25 growth attributed partly to 'deeper penetration in core markets and calibrated expansion in newer regions of the West and South' and expanding footprint into Tier-III/Tier-IV towns.

china_plus_one.evidence: News/analyst coverage (not primary AR text, WebFetch to IR/PDF sources blocked in this session): Garware is described as 'the top exporter of PPF in the world,' selling to 75+ countries, with exports ~74-81% of revenue and the US/Americas the largest market (~55% of revenue in Q2FY25 vs 33% in FY22). DGTR recommended anti-dumping duty on TPU-based PPF imports from China into India, and Garware is positioned to benefit as global PPF demand shifts toward non-Chinese suppliers. No explicit 'China+1' phrase was found in the primary source, hence moderate rather than strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Analyst commentary: primary raw materials are petrochemical derivatives (Purified Terephthalic Acid, Mono-ethylene glycol, polypropylene) whose prices move with crude oil; Garware sources from Indian refiners (e.g. Reliance Industries) at import-parity pricing and passes on RM cost increases to customers with a lag, especially in value-added segments. No exact raw-material-cost % disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (largely USD-denominated, Americas ~55% of revenue) account for ~74-81% of consolidated revenue per third-party sources, implying material USD revenue exposure, but no explicit disclosed USD-revenue % or hedging policy was located within the fetch budget.

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield/Eicher Motors is predominantly a domestic two-wheeler business; no China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Analyst/news commentary (not primary AR MD&A text): 'Analysts remain upbeat on Eicher Motors owing to domestic demand aided by government-led consumption measures (income tax relief/GST rate cuts) and a rural demand uptick, and new model launches' -- no rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported a net cash position of roughly Rs 24.8 billion (debt ~Rs 4.04bn vs cash ~Rs 28.8bn) as of late FY25 with debt-to-equity around 0.02, indicating minimal borrowings and low sensitivity to rate movements. No floating-rate liability % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: International revenue was ~54% of FY25 total sales (domestic Rs 3,660 cr vs international Rs 4,236 cr of Rs 7,896 cr total), with international revenue up 20.5% YoY driven by growth in Canada and emerging markets. No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing was found in sources reviewed, so classified as 'weak' (export business present, no diversification narrative).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge: offsets foreign-currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign-currency receivables
inr_exposure.evidence: CARE Ratings press release on Emcure (third-party, not primary AR text): 'Emcure manages currency exposure from fluctuations in exchange rates by offsetting foreign currency payables -- such as trade obligations and loans -- against foreign currency receivables, creating a natural hedge.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharma was approved in Group B under the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (bulk drugs/API-linked incentive scheme), alongside Biocon, MSN Labs and Wockhardt. No revenue % attributable to PLI disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Netweb is overwhelmingly a domestic (Make-in-India / import-substitution) IT hardware business; management commentary indicates export revenue is only ~5-6% of revenue currently, targeted to reach ~10% within 2-3 years. No China+1 export-diversification narrative found; the company's own positioning is around import substitution (reducing India's dependence on imported IT hardware) rather than customers diversifying away from China to source from Netweb for export markets.

govt_capex.evidence: Government and defense are meaningful customer segments: AI-systems revenue mix was ~23-24% government vs ~76-77% enterprise; Space & Defence segment revenue grew 283% YoY to ~Rs 83.4 crore, including a large AI order executed in the defense sector. Total-company government-revenue % not explicitly disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb Technologies received a Production Linked Incentive of approximately Rs 5.93-5.94 crore under the Government of India's PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, for the period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024 -- the company's first claim under the scheme. Incentive amount not expressed as a % of revenue in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Q3 FY25 management commentary noted 'subdued demand across urban and rural geographies' with steady volume growth; management expressed cautious optimism on rural demand recovery aided by good monsoon and construction activity. No specific rural revenue % disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Analyst/press commentary indicates VAM (vinyl acetate monomer), a crude-oil derivative, accounts for roughly 50-60% of Pidilite's raw material costs; VAM requirement is met largely via imports and VAM cost per tonne has risen from ~$750 to ~$1,300. Figure not confirmed against the primary AR text (source unreachable).

china_plus_one.evidence: Coverage of Sona Comstar's FY25/FY26 results describes 'growing traction in Eastern markets' (59% of revenue vs 56% a year earlier) and record EV order/order-book growth attributed to geographic and product diversification (e.g. 'EV orders and diversification drive growth'); company is expanding into China, Japan and South Korea and operates plants in India, USA, Mexico and China. No explicit 'China+1' framing found in the excerpts reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company described as relying heavily on North America and Europe (~66% combined) for revenue with India ~28%, and 'over 50% of its sales are for international markets' via 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities in India, USA, Mexico and China; explicit hedging policy text not located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar (Sona BLW) received certification under India's auto PLI scheme for a hub-wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers, reported as the first automotive component manufacturer to receive such certification (BusinessToday, Feb 2024).

rural.evidence: Q3 FY25 CMD commentary: the quarter was 'marked by food inflation and moderation in urban consumption, with a gradual recovery in rural consumption'; company stated it is targeting deeper penetration of 'RUrban' (rural-urban) markets via e-commerce. No specific rural revenue % disclosed in the FY24-25 AR sources reviewed (an older, FY22-era management statement had cited ~20-25% of sales from rural markets, but this predates the FY24-25 report and was not used).

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestlé India's proposal under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), covering Ready-to-Eat/Ready-to-Cook foods and processed fruits & vegetables, was approved by the Government of India in December 2021 and the scheme runs through FY2026-27; revenue impact not separately quantified in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company hedges forecasted/predictable foreign-currency cash flows using forward contracts (per press/analyst commentary reporting hedge losses of ~$10M in a quarter and a further ~$14M mark-to-market loss expected to be realized over the following two quarters). Exact FY24-25 USD revenue % not located.
inr_exposure.evidence: North America (Americas) reported as ~53.9% of FY25 revenue (down slightly from ~55% in FY24) and EMEA ~34.7% of FY25 revenue, per analyst/press summaries. Note: this is the Americas/North America geographic segment, not a pure US-only figure. India is reported as a separate geographic segment but its FY25 % of total revenue was not found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Third-party analysis describes a pan-India distribution network of 60,000+ retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban/rural penetration; Country Liquor targets price-sensitive rural consumers; 'regular' segment (typically rural/semi-urban) volumes grew 79.6% YoY in a recent quarter after nine quarters of decline. No explicit rural revenue % disclosed in sources found.
Only generic industry-level commentary found (gold demand in rural India picks up post-harvest); no Titan-specific rural revenue disclosure located.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported to use forward contracts and options to hedge USD/EUR exposure (third-party analysis, not directly verified in AR text)
inr_exposure.evidence: Third-party summary: 'Aurobindo Pharma earns over 70% of revenues in USD and EUR while reporting in INR... uses forward contracts and options to hedge exposure.' Separately, US formulations reported at 47-51.1% of consolidated revenue in FY25; international markets overall reported at 89% of revenue mix vs 11% domestic.

pli_scheme.evidence: Invested ~Rs 2,400 crore in a Penicillin-G (Pen-G) manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh approved under India's PLI Scheme, with annual capacity of ~15,000 tonnes; company was ramping large-scale Pen-G commercialization in FY25.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst commentary (Jefferies) attributes Divi's custom-synthesis growth (~16% CAGR guided through FY28) to 'China+1 tailwinds and Big Pharma partnerships' as US/EU pharma diversify sourcing away from China; management has noted RFQ-to-pilot-project conversions in this context, though large financial benefit was described as still materializing. Not confirmed as a direct verbatim AR quote.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company disclosed concentrated sourcing risk for key inputs including methanol, imported solvents, and Middle-East-sourced materials, and monitors effects of US tariffs on China-origin suppliers and Russia sanctions on raw material/intermediate/solvent costs. No explicit % of raw materials tied to crude oil found; mitigants cited include diversified sourcing, long-term customer contracts with cost pass-through mechanisms, and backward integration (Unit 3, Kakinada).

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports comprised ~88-90% of FY25 sales revenue, with Europe ~52-56% and North America ~16-17% of total revenue; remainder from India (~12%), Asia (~11%), and Rest of World (~4%).

FY25 segmental revenue: Domestic ₹2,269 Cr, International ₹1,128 Cr, CDMO ₹446 Cr, API ₹76 Cr (~58% domestic / 42% international). Company exports formulations to 40+ countries with strong presence in Russia, Ukraine and other CIS markets; international formulation revenue growth cited as driven by Russia and branded generics exports.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/company commentary: 'Uno Minda can leverage PLI and localization incentives to improve margin and defend share versus China-origin suppliers.' Global network supported by JVs/technical agreements with automakers in Japan, South Korea, Germany and China. This is framed as import-substitution/localization vs. China rather than an explicit export-driven China+1 diversification narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Rubber, plastic and aluminium inputs used in Uno Minda's components are petrochemical/commodity-linked (rubber/plastic derived from crude feedstocks such as butadiene, styrene, polyethylene, polypropylene); no company-disclosed % of raw material cost tied to crude was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Total international business (physical exports + overseas operations) cited at approximately 9-10% of consolidated revenue in recent quarters (FY26); ~₹500-600 Cr of 9-month physical exports from India cited in one analyst note.

pli_scheme.evidence: Uno Minda listed among 10 Component Champion applicants certified under the Auto PLI scheme's Component Champion Incentive Scheme (37 AAT component variants certified). Company commentary notes 'no PLI benefit accrued in Q3 or 9M FY26,' indicating certification achieved but incentive not yet booked to P&L.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 geographic revenue mix ~52% export / 48% domestic. Major FY25 institutional/export orders: ₹18.20 crore from UNFPA (male/female condoms) and ₹14.91 crore from Government of Tanzania. Company secured maximum allocation in South Africa's 5-year national condom procurement programme (RT75-2025) — 23.40 million female condoms/yr (59% share) and 153 million male condom pieces/yr — providing annual revenue visibility of approx. $12.98 million (~₹115 crore) from Dec 2025. Long-term supply agreements with WHO/UNFPA/PFSCM cited as securing a substantial share of international revenue.

crude_exposure.evidence: Endurance is an aluminium die-casting specialist (suspension, brake and transmission components); analyst commentary notes aluminium/commodity cost exposure but no company-disclosed % of raw material cost tied to crude was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue split approx. 75.8% India, 23.6% Europe (Italy and Germany subsidiaries), 0.6% Maxwell; company operates 19 plants in India and 14 in Europe. Export sales growth in prior periods (e.g. Q2FY24 +12.6% YoY) attributed partly to machine casting sales to Ford (UK) and IVECO (Italy). Aftermarket exports grew 29% in FY25 per company commentary; aftermarket sales targeted at 10% of domestic revenue by FY28.

pli_scheme.evidence: Third-party analyst commentary: 'Endurance's leadership in aluminium die-casting positions it as a primary beneficiary of regulatory safety mandates, PLI scheme and electrification' within India's Auto PLI framework; no company-disclosed % of revenue from PLI incentives was found.
